description: A Vietnamese hotel maid is brought to California by a woman determined to find her autistic son a wife. Hoang writes the mother as more than a device.

title: Act Your Age, Eve Brown
description: A drifting youngest sister hits a rigid bed-and-breakfast owner with her car and ends up working for him with his arm in a sling. Both leads are autistic, and neither is a lesson.

title: Boyfriend Material
description: A charity worker with a bad tabloid reputation fake-dates a rigorously boring barrister to fix it. Very funny, and quietly serious about being the child of famous parents.

title: Written in the Stars
description: An astrologer and an actuary who does not believe in any of it fake a relationship for the holidays. Sapphic rom-com built on a very old chassis, cheerfully.

title: The Charm Offensive
description: The star of a Bachelor-style dating show falls for the producer assigned to make him likeable. Kinder about anxiety and medication than most romances manage.

title: Under the Whispering Door
description: A dead lawyer is delivered to a tea shop that serves as a waystation, and refuses to walk through the door. A romance about being reluctant to have lived badly.

title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
description: A caseworker for magical children is sent to inspect an orphanage on an island, including one child who is the literal Antichrist. Gentle to a degree that is nearly a thesis.

title: The Hunger Games
description: Katniss Everdeen volunteers for a televised fight to the death so her sister will not have to. Collins wrote it thinking about reality television and the Iraq war, and it shows in the coverage more than the combat.

title: Catching Fire
description: Victory makes Katniss a symbol the Capitol cannot control and cannot kill outright. The middle book, where the series turns from survival to insurrection.

title: Mockingjay
description: The rebellion needs Katniss on camera more than in the field. An unusually bleak ending for a bestselling trilogy, and pointedly unsatisfying about what war leaves.

title: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes
description: The tenth Hunger Games, mentored by an eighteen-year-old Coriolanus Snow. A prequel that declines to make its future dictator sympathetic for long.

title: Divergent
description: A Chicago sorted into five factions by disposition, and a girl who fits none of them. The most successful of the many books that followed The Hunger Games.

title: The Maze Runner
description: Boys with no memories wake in a walled glade beside a maze that rearranges itself nightly. Puzzle-box premise, and the questions are better than the answers.

title: The Giver
description: A boy in a community without colour, weather or pain is assigned to receive its memories. The book that taught a generation what a dystopia was, at about eleven.

title: Unwind
description: A civil war over abortion ends in a compromise: children between thirteen and eighteen can be retroactively terminated by having every part of them transplanted. Follows three teenagers running.

title: Scythe
description: In a world that has cured death, a licensed order of scythes must kill to control population. Two teenagers are apprenticed and told only one will be chosen.

title: Legend
description: A military prodigy hunts the Republic's most wanted criminal, who is fifteen and from the slums. Told in alternating voices that converge on the same lie.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
description: An orphan living in a cupboard learns on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard. Whatever its later reputation, it reorganised children's publishing entirely.

title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
description: An escaped prisoner is hunting Harry, and the truth about his parents' betrayal is not what he was told. Usually named the best-constructed book in the series.

title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
description: A schools tournament with three lethal tasks, and an ending that turns the series from adventure into war. The point where the books got long and dark.

title: The Lightning Thief
description: A dyslexic twelve-year-old discovers he is the son of Poseidon and is accused of stealing Zeus's master bolt. Greek myth relocated to summer camp, very funny about it.

title: Northern Lights
description: Lyra Belacqua leaves Oxford for the ice, chasing stolen children and a substance the Church would rather nobody understood. Sold in America as The Golden Compass.

title: The Subtle Knife
description: Lyra meets a boy from our Oxford and a knife that cuts windows between worlds. The trilogy's argument with Paradise Lost becomes explicit.

title: A Wrinkle in Time
description: Three children travel by tesseract to rescue a scientist father from a planet where every house is identical. Rejected by dozens of publishers for being too strange for children.

title: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
description: Four evacuated children find a country in permanent winter through the back of a wardrobe. The Christian allegory is not hidden, and the snow is still the best thing in it.

title: The Hobbit
description: A comfortable hobbit is bullied into a dragon-burglary by thirteen dwarves and a wizard. Written for Tolkien's children and much lighter than what it led to.

title: The Amber Spyglass
description: The trilogy's conclusion goes to the land of the dead and stages a second Fall. Divisive, ambitious, and unusually willing to make its child readers grieve.

title: The Fault in Our Stars
description: Two teenagers meet at a cancer support group and go to Amsterdam to confront a novelist. Green refuses to make either of them noble about dying.

title: Looking for Alaska
description: A boy at an Alabama boarding school falls for a girl who is more damaged than he can see. Structured as a countdown to something, then an aftermath.

title: The Perks of Being a Wallflower
description: A freshman writes letters to a stranger about his first year, his friends, and something he has not let himself remember. Frequently banned, and read anyway.

title: Speak
description: A girl who called the police at a summer party is frozen out of her freshman year and stops speaking. Anderson writes the silence as a physical condition.

title: The Hate U Give
description: A sixteen-year-old is the only witness when a police officer shoots her childhood friend. Moves between her Black neighbourhood and her mostly white school.

title: Eleanor & Park
description: Two misfits share a school bus seat in 1986 Omaha, then comics, then a mixtape. The home Eleanor is escaping is drawn without any softening.

title: Fangirl
description: A twin who writes enormously popular fan fiction starts university without her sister. Rowell takes fandom seriously as a way of being a person.

title: Simon vs. the Homo Sapiens Agenda
description: A closeted sixteen-year-old emailing an anonymous classmate is blackmailed by someone who found the messages. Warm, and specific about the theft of being outed.

title: Aristotle and Dante Discover the Secrets of the Universe
description: Two Mexican-American boys meet at a swimming pool in 1987 El Paso. Slow, quiet, and as much about their fathers as about each other.

title: I'll Give You the Sun
description: Twins tell alternating halves of the same story three years apart, one before their mother's death and one after. The prose is extravagant and mostly earns it.

title: We Were Liars
description: A wealthy family's private island, four teenagers, and a summer the narrator cannot remember. Built entirely around a withheld fact.

title: One of Us Is Lying
description: Five students go into detention and one dies. The Breakfast Club with a murder investigation, and each of the four suspects had a secret worth killing over.

title: Sadie
description: A girl hunting her sister's killer, told against a true-crime podcast retracing her route. The podcast format is used for more than novelty.

title: Long Way Down
description: Sixty seconds in a lift, a boy with his brother's gun, and a floor-by-floor visitation by the dead. Written in verse and read in an hour.

title: The Book Thief
description: A foster girl in Nazi Germany steals books and reads them in a basement to a hidden Jewish man. Narrated by Death, who is tired and not unkind.

title: The Outsiders
description: Greasers and Socs in 1960s Oklahoma, and the night that ends in a body. Hinton was seventeen when she wrote it, which is why the voices land.

title: A Monster Calls
description: A yew tree walks to a boy's window at seven minutes past midnight to tell him three stories and demand a fourth. His mother is dying. Devastating and short.

title: The Knife of Never Letting Go
description: A colony where every man's thoughts are audible, and a boy who finds a pocket of silence in the swamp. The typography does real work in the noise.

title: Six of Crows
description: Six criminals are hired for an impossible prison break in a mercantile city built on gambling debt. A heist novel with six points of view and no wasted one.

title: Shadow and Bone
description: An orphan mapmaker discovers she can summon light and is taken to court to be trained as its saviour. Russian-inflected fantasy, and the setting outlasted the plot.

title: The Cruel Prince
description: A human girl raised in the faerie court by the man who murdered her parents decides to make herself indispensable. Vicious court politics, and the romance is not comfortable.

title: An Ember in the Ashes
description: A slave in a Roman-inflected empire and a soldier who hates what he is being trained into. Alternating voices, and the empire is genuinely brutal.

title: Children of Blood and Bone
description: A West African-inspired kingdom where magic was destroyed and its practitioners' descendants are marked by white hair. A quest to bring it back, pursued by the crown prince.

title: The Poppy War
description: A war orphan tests into an elite military academy, then into a war modelled closely on the Second Sino-Japanese War. Begins as a school story and does not stay one.

title: A Darker Shade of Magic
description: Four Londons layered on each other, and one of the last magicians able to walk between them. The smuggling is what starts the trouble.

title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
description: A woman trades her soul for immortality and is cursed to be forgotten by everyone she meets. Three hundred years later a man in a bookshop remembers her.

title: Eragon
description: A farm boy finds a dragon egg. Paolini was fifteen when he wrote it and the influences are visible, which did nothing to slow it down.

title: Graceling
description: A girl whose Grace appears to be killing is used as her uncle's enforcer until she learns what her ability actually is. The romance refuses marriage on principle.

title: The Ruby in the Smoke
description: A sixteen-year-old in 1872 London investigates her father's drowning and a phrase that kills a man on hearing it. Opium, pawnbrokers and a very capable heroine.

title: Howl's Moving Castle
description: A hatmaker cursed into an old woman's body takes work as a cleaner in a wandering wizard's castle. Funnier and more intricate than the film, and differently plotted.

title: Coraline
description: A bored girl finds a door to a flat exactly like her own, where her other mother has buttons for eyes and would like her to stay. Genuinely frightening at any age.

title: The Graveyard Book
description: A toddler whose family is murdered is raised by the dead in a graveyard. The Jungle Book restaged among headstones, chapter by chapter as he grows.

title: Holes
description: A boy wrongly convicted is sent to a desert camp where boys dig a hole a day. Three timelines converge with unusual precision for a children's book.

title: Bridge to Terabithia
description: Two lonely children invent a kingdom in the woods across a creek. Then one of them crosses alone. Still one of the most frequently challenged books in American schools.

title: The Westing Game
description: Sixteen heirs are paired off and given clues to a millionaire's death, with the estate going to whoever solves it. A fair-play mystery that trusts children to keep up.

title: Matilda
description: A gifted child with contemptible parents and a monstrous headmistress discovers she can move things with her mind. Dahl at his most gleefully unfair to adults.

title: Charlotte's Web
description: A spider saves a pig by writing about him in her web. White wrote the plainest possible sentences about death and it has never stopped working.

title: Anne of Green Gables
description: An orphan sent by mistake to a Prince Edward Island farm that asked for a boy. Talkative, imaginative, and much sharper about being unwanted than its reputation suggests.

title: Little Women
description: Four sisters in Civil War Massachusetts, and Jo March refusing the plot everyone has for her. Alcott wrote it for money and resented the marriages her publisher demanded.

title: The Secret Garden
description: A sour orphan sent to a Yorkshire manor finds a walled garden nobody has entered in ten years. Two unpleasant children become tolerable through gardening, roughly.

title: The Phantom Tollbooth
description: A bored boy drives a toy car through a tollbooth into a land where words and numbers are at war. Almost entirely puns, and the puns are load-bearing.

title: Wonder
description: A boy with a facial difference starts fifth grade after years of homeschooling. Told from several viewpoints, including the sister everyone forgets.

title: The Crossover
description: Twin basketball players and their father's failing heart, written in verse that moves at the speed of the game. Won the Newbery on the strength of its rhythm.

title: Brown Girl Dreaming
description: Woodson's childhood between South Carolina and Brooklyn in the 1960s and 70s, in verse. About segregation, family, and taking a long time to learn to read.

title: New Kid
description: A Black seventh-grader is sent to a wealthy private school instead of art school. The first graphic novel to win the Newbery, and precise about small daily indignities.

title: Smile
description: Telgemeier knocks out her front teeth in sixth grade and spends years in orthodontics while her friendships curdle. Autobiographical, and hugely influential on the shelf.

title: El Deafo
description: Bell's childhood deafness and the bulky hearing aid she reimagined as a superpower. Funny about the exhaustion of lip-reading a whole classroom.

title: The Tale of Despereaux
description: A mouse with oversized ears who loves a princess, a rat who loves light, and a serving girl who wants a crown. Narrated directly to the reader, sometimes sternly.

title: Because of Winn-Dixie
description: A preacher's daughter adopts a stray dog in a Florida town and collects its lonely adults. Slight on plot and unusually good on loneliness.

title: The Sea of Monsters
description: Percy sails the Sea of Monsters for the Golden Fleece to save the camp's magical border. The Odyssey compressed into a summer road trip.

title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid
description: A middle-schooler's illustrated journal, in which he is consistently the least sympathetic person in every anecdote he tells. Enormously popular with the age it mocks.

title: Where the Crawdads Sing
description: A girl raised alone in the North Carolina marshes becomes the suspect in a local man's death. Half courtroom procedural, half natural history, and it sold like almost nothing else that decade.

title: Little Fires Everywhere
description: A planned Ohio suburb, a tenant artist who will not follow its rules, and a custody fight over a Chinese-American baby. Ng is interested in what respectability costs.

title: Everything I Never Told You
description: A mixed-race family in 1970s Ohio after the middle daughter is found in the lake. Opens with the death and works backwards through everyone's silence.

title: A Little Life
description: Four college friends in New York over decades, narrowing onto one man's history of abuse. Long, relentless, and genuinely divisive about whether the suffering is earned.

title: The Goldfinch
description: A boy survives the museum bombing that kills his mother and walks out with a Dutch painting. Dickensian in shape and length, and it won the Pulitzer.

title: A Man Called Ove
description: A widower with rigid views about parking and inferior cars keeps being interrupted in his attempts to die by the family that moved in next door.

title: Anxious People
description: A failed bank robber takes an apartment viewing hostage and the witnesses cannot agree on anything. Comic, then abruptly not.

title: Eleanor Oliphant Is Completely Fine
description: A meticulous, deeply isolated office worker begins, reluctantly, to have a life. The comedy of her literal-mindedness runs directly into what happened to her face.

title: The Midnight Library
description: A woman between life and death browses a library of the lives she might have lived. Schematic on purpose, and it reached an enormous number of people at the right moment.

title: Lessons in Chemistry
description: A chemist pushed out of research in 1960s California ends up presenting a cookery programme and teaching housewives thermodynamics. Angrier than its packaging.

title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
description: Two friends make video games together for thirty years and never quite manage to be a couple or to stop. Serious about games as a form.

title: Demon Copperhead
description: David Copperfield relocated to the Virginia mountains during the opioid epidemic, narrated by a boy passed between foster placements. Won the Pulitzer.

title: The Poisonwood Bible
description: A Baptist missionary drags his wife and four daughters to the Belgian Congo in 1959. Narrated by the five women, none of whom forgive him.

title: The Kite Runner
description: A Kabul boyhood, a betrayal in an alley, and a return decades later under the Taliban. The book that put Afghanistan on Western book club tables.

title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
description: Two women married to the same man in Kabul across three decades of war. Harder than The Kite Runner and better constructed.

title: Life of Pi
description: A boy adrift in a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger for 227 days, and then a second account of the same voyage. The ending asks which story you prefer.

title: The Help
description: Black maids in 1960s Jackson, Mississippi tell their stories to a young white writer. Hugely popular and heavily criticised for centring the white author-figure.

title: The Secret Life of Bees
description: A white girl in 1964 South Carolina runs away with her Black housekeeper and is taken in by three beekeeping sisters. Sweet-natured about a violent year.

title: The Immortalists
description: Four siblings are told the dates of their deaths by a fortune teller in 1969 and live the next fifty years accordingly. One life per section.

title: Commonwealth
description: A kiss at a christening breaks two marriages and mixes six children. Fifty years of the consequences, told out of order.

title: Bel Canto
description: Terrorists take a diplomatic party hostage in South America and the siege lasts months, during which everyone becomes attached to a visiting soprano.

title: The Dutch House
description: A brother and sister sit in a parked car outside the house they were expelled from, for decades. A fairy tale about a stepmother, told realistically.

title: Pachinko
description: Four generations of a Korean family in Japan, where they remain foreigners regardless of how long they stay. Opens in 1910 and does not stop for eighty years.

title: Homegoing
description: Two half-sisters in eighteenth-century Ghana, one married to a slaver and one sold. Then a chapter per descendant, alternating across three hundred years.

title: The Vanishing Half
description: Twin sisters from a Louisiana town of light-skinned Black families run away at sixteen; one returns and one passes as white for the rest of her life.

title: An American Marriage
description: A year into a marriage, the husband is wrongly convicted and sentenced to twelve years. Told partly in letters, and it refuses to make the wife's waiting simple.

title: Such a Fun Age
description: A Black babysitter is accused of kidnapping in a supermarket, and her white employer decides to make it right. Excruciatingly precise about good intentions.

title: Americanah
description: A Nigerian woman blogs about American race from the outside while her first love builds a life in London. Adichie on hair, class and what emigration does to a couple.

title: The Sympathizer
description: A communist double agent embedded with South Vietnamese officers in Los Angeles writes a confession. Furious, funny, and won the Pulitzer.

title: There There
description: Twelve Native characters converging on a powwow in Oakland. Urban rather than reservation, which is the point Orange opens the book by making.

title: The Overstory
description: Nine strangers drawn into the defence of the last old-growth forests. Structured like a tree, and it changed how a lot of readers look at one.

title: Sea of Tranquility
description: 1912 Vancouver Island, a 2203 moon colony, and a novelist on tour during a plague. A time-travel investigation that keeps returning to the same few seconds in a forest.

title: The Glass Hotel
description: A Ponzi scheme, a remote hotel in British Columbia, and a woman who disappears from a container ship. Mandel writes money as haunting.

title: Cloud Cuckoo Land
description: A lost Greek manuscript links the siege of Constantinople, an Idaho library, and a generation ship. Doerr on books as the thing that survives.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
description: A blind French girl and a German boy conscripted for his talent with radios, converging on Saint-Malo in 1944. Short chapters, and it won the Pulitzer.

title: The Tattooist of Auschwitz
description: A Slovakian Jew assigned to tattoo numbers on arrivals falls in love with a woman in the queue. Based on interviews, and historians have disputed a good deal of it.

title: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida
description: A dead war photographer has seven moons to solve his own murder in 1990 Colombo. Won the Booker; the afterlife has queues and bureaucracy.

title: Shuggie Bain
description: A boy in 1980s Glasgow looking after his alcoholic mother while everyone else leaves. Won the Booker, and it is as hard as that summary sounds.

title: Hamnet
description: The death of Shakespeare's eleven-year-old son, told from his wife's side and barely mentioning the playwright by name. The plague chapter is extraordinary.

title: Klara and the Sun
description: A solar-powered artificial friend in a shop window is bought for a sick girl. Narrated by Klara, whose understanding of what she sees is partial and touching.

title: Lincoln in the Bardo
description: Willie Lincoln's night in a Georgetown crypt, narrated by the dead and by fragments of real historical sources. Won the Booker; formally unlike anything else.

title: The Nickel Boys
description: A boy bound for college is sent instead to a Florida reform school modelled on the real Dozier School. Spare, and the structure withholds one thing.

title: The Underground Railroad
description: The railroad rendered as a literal train under the ground, and each state a different experiment in American racism. Won the Pulitzer.

title: If We Were Villains
description: Seven Shakespeare students at an elite conservatory, one body, and a narrator telling it ten years later from prison. Dark academia, openly in Tartt's debt.

title: Rules of Civility
description: A typist's year in 1938 Manhattan after a chance meeting in a jazz bar on New Year's Eve. Towles on the American self-invention machine.

title: The Lincoln Highway
description: Four boys in 1954 set out from Nebraska for California and go east instead. Ten days, several narrators, and a mounting sense of a mistake.

title: The Thursday Murder Club
description: Four residents of a retirement village who meet weekly over cold cases get a live one. Funny, and clear-eyed about being old and underestimated.

title: The Man Who Died Twice
description: Elizabeth's first husband turns up having stolen twenty million in diamonds from the wrong people. The second Thursday Murder Club, with a higher body count.

title: The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency
description: Precious Ramotswe sells her father's cattle to open Botswana's first female detective agency. The cases are small and the book is about the country.

title: Still Life
description: Chief Inspector Gamache investigates an archery death in a Quebec village that is not on any map. The village is the reason the series has eighteen more.

title: Magpie Murders
description: An editor reads a golden-age detective novel with the last chapter missing, then has to solve her author's death to find it. Two mysteries, nested.

title: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
description: The same day at a country house repeats, with the investigator waking in a different guest's body each time. A locked-room mystery crossed with a logic problem.

title: The House of the Spirits
description: Three generations of the Trueba family through a century of Chilean politics, ending in the coup. Ghosts and clairvoyance sit beside torture without apology.

title: The Shadow of the Wind
description: A boy in postwar Barcelona chooses a book from the Cemetery of Forgotten Books and finds someone has been burning every other copy.

title: The Elegance of the Hedgehog
description: A concierge hiding her erudition and a twelve-year-old planning suicide, in the same Paris building. Both change when a Japanese tenant moves in.

title: My Brilliant Friend
description: Two girls in a poor Naples neighbourhood in the 1950s, one of whom is allowed to keep going to school. The first of four, and the friendship is not sentimental.

title: The Days of Abandonment
description: A woman comes apart over a Turin summer after her husband leaves. Short and much more violent in feeling than the Neapolitan novels.

title: Convenience Store Woman
description: A woman who has worked the same Tokyo convenience store for eighteen years and is perfectly content is pressured into a life she is supposed to want.

title: Before the Coffee Gets Cold
description: A Tokyo café where one seat sends you back in time, on strict conditions, and nothing you do can change the present. Four linked stories about saying the thing anyway.

title: The Housekeeper and the Professor
description: A mathematician whose memory lasts eighty minutes, his housekeeper, and her son. They communicate mostly in number theory, which is more moving than it sounds.

title: Norwegian Wood
description: A student in late-sixties Tokyo between the withdrawn girlfriend of his dead best friend and someone entirely alive. Murakami's most straightforwardly realist novel.

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
description: A man looking for his wife's cat, then his wife, descends a dry well and into Japan's occupation of Manchuria. Enormous and deliberately unresolved.

title: The Ministry of Utmost Happiness
description: A hijra who moves into a Delhi graveyard, and a woman connected to the Kashmir insurgency. Roy's second novel, twenty years after the first, and much angrier.

title: A Suitable Boy
description: A mother's search for a husband for her daughter in newly independent India, across 1,300 pages of four families and a general election.

title: White Teeth
description: Two wartime friends and their families in north London over fifty years. Smith was twenty-four, and the book is as loud and crowded as the city it describes.

title: On Beauty
description: Two feuding academic families in a New England college town. Howards End restaged around affirmative action and a Rembrandt argument.

title: Brooklyn
description: A young woman sent from Enniscorthy to 1950s Brooklyn builds a life, then is called home. Very quiet, and the last fifty pages are agonising.

title: Oryx and Crake
description: The last man alive remembers the friend who engineered the plague and the corporate compounds they grew up in. Atwood's other dystopia, and the more prescient one.

title: The Testaments
description: Gilead fifteen years on, told by three women including Aunt Lydia. Written after the television series and much more interested in how a regime rots from inside.

title: The Power
description: Teenage girls develop the ability to deliver electric shocks and the world's power balance inverts within a decade. Framed as a historical novel written far in the future.

title: Severance
description: A New York publishing drone keeps going to the office through a fever that leaves its victims repeating routines until they die. Satire of work, written before 2020.

title: Blood Meridian
description: A boy rides with a scalp-hunting gang across the 1850s borderlands, alongside Judge Holden. Frequently called the great American novel and almost unreadably violent.

title: No Country for Old Men
description: A welder takes two million dollars from a drug deal in the desert and is hunted by a man with a cattle gun. Stripped to dialogue and consequence.

title: Lonesome Dove
description: Two retired Texas Rangers drive cattle from the Rio Grande to Montana. Won the Pulitzer, and it is the book that made the western respectable again.

title: The Son
description: Three generations of a Texas dynasty from Comanche captivity to oil. Told in rotation, and each generation's wealth rests on the previous one's atrocity.

title: East of Eden
description: Two families in the Salinas Valley replaying Cain and Abel across generations. Steinbeck thought it his best; the word timshel does a lot of the work.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
description: The Joads driven from Oklahoma to California by dust and the banks. Burned publicly on publication, won the Pulitzer, and remains hard to argue with.

title: Of Mice and Men
description: Two migrant workers with a plan for a small farm, and a man who does not know his own strength. A hundred pages, and the ending is visible from the first.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
description: A lawyer defends a Black man against a rape charge in 1930s Alabama, narrated by his young daughter. The most assigned novel in American schools, for better and worse.

title: The Great Gatsby
description: A bootlegger throws parties across the bay from the woman he reorganised his life around. Short, and almost every sentence is doing something.

title: Their Eyes Were Watching God
description: Janie Crawford's three marriages, told to a friend on a porch. Dismissed on publication, recovered decades later, and the dialect is the achievement.

title: The Color Purple
description: Letters from a Black woman in rural Georgia, first to God and then to her sister. Won the Pulitzer and is still routinely banned.

title: Song of Solomon
description: A man called Milkman traces his family south and finds a story about flight. Morrison's third novel and the one that made her reputation.

title: Sula
description: Two girls in an Ohio hill town, one who leaves and one who stays, and the betrayal between them. Under two hundred pages and it holds a whole community.

title: A Visit from the Goon Squad
description: Thirteen linked chapters around a record executive and his assistant, jumping decades and voices, including one told entirely in PowerPoint. Won the Pulitzer.

title: The Corrections
description: A mother wants her three adult children home for one last Christmas while her husband's Parkinson's advances. Franzen on the Midwest and the market, at length.

title: Freedom
description: A liberal St Paul couple, their best friend the rock musician, and a mountaintop-removal conservation deal. Suburban decency examined until it cracks.

title: Middlesex
description: Three generations of a Greek-American family in Detroit, narrated by an intersex man tracing a recessive gene from a village on Mount Olympus. Won the Pulitzer.

title: The Virgin Suicides
description: Five sisters in 1970s Michigan, remembered decades later by the neighbourhood boys who watched them and understood nothing. Narrated in the collective we.

title: Olive Kitteridge
description: Thirteen stories in a coastal Maine town, all touching a retired maths teacher who is difficult in ways the book never smooths over. Won the Pulitzer.

title: My Name Is Lucy Barton
description: A woman in a New York hospital is visited by the mother she has not spoken to in years. Five days of talk that avoids everything important.

title: Gilead
description: A dying Iowa preacher writes a long letter to the young son who will not remember him. Won the Pulitzer, and it is almost entirely interior.

title: Housekeeping
description: Two orphaned sisters raised by a drifting aunt in an Idaho lake town. Robinson's first novel and its sentences are the reason people talk about it.

title: Stoner
description: The unremarkable life of a Missouri farm boy who becomes an English professor. Ignored on publication, rediscovered fifty years later, and quietly devastating.

title: The Girl on the Train
description: A blackout drinker who watches the same house from the same commuter train every morning becomes a witness to a disappearance she cannot remember. Three narrators, all of them lying.

title: The Silent Patient
description: A painter shoots her husband and never speaks again; the therapist who takes her case is more invested than he admits. Built entirely around one reveal.

title: Behind Closed Doors
description: A couple everyone envies, and a wife who is never left alone with anyone. Alternates between the courtship and the house she cannot leave.

title: The Woman in the Window
description: An agoraphobic child psychologist drinking through old films believes she has watched a murder across the street. Rear Window with a narrator nobody believes, including herself.

title: Big Little Lies
description: Three mothers at an Australian primary school, building toward a death at a trivia night. The gossip chorus between chapters is the best device in it.

title: The Husband's Secret
description: A woman finds a letter from her husband to be opened after his death. He is alive. Three women's lives converge on what it says.

title: The Couple Next Door
description: A couple leave the baby monitor on and go to dinner next door. The baby is gone when they get back, and neither of them is telling the police everything.

title: The Last Thing He Told Me
description: A man vanishes leaving a note reading protect her, and his wife and hostile stepdaughter go looking for who he actually was.

title: The Wife Between Us
description: A discarded first wife watches her ex-husband's engagement to a younger woman. The book depends on you assuming you know which is which.

title: Before I Go to Sleep
description: A woman whose memory resets every night keeps a journal her husband does not know about. Each morning she reads what she no longer knows.

title: Sharp Objects
description: A reporter returns to her Missouri hometown to cover two dead girls and stays with the mother she has been avoiding. Flynn's first, and the meanest.

title: Dark Places
description: The sole survivor of a family massacre, whose testimony convicted her brother, is paid by true-crime hobbyists to reopen it. Kansas farm foreclosure as backdrop.

title: The Likeness
description: A detective goes undercover as a murder victim who was using an identity she herself invented, moving into the house the dead woman shared with four students.

title: Broken Harbour
description: A family attacked in a half-built ghost estate outside Dublin after the crash, with holes punched through the walls. French on what the recession did to people.

title: The Cuckoo's Calling
description: A one-legged veteran turned private detective investigates a supermodel's fall from a balcony. Published pseudonymously and better for having been read cold.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
description: A disgraced journalist and a hacker with a state guardian investigate a disappearance on a private island forty years cold. The book that exported Nordic noir.

title: The Girl Who Played with Fire
description: Salander is named for three murders and goes underground while Blomkvist tries to prove otherwise. Her history stops being background.

title: The Snowman
description: Harry Hole hunts a killer who leaves a snowman outside the houses of the women he takes. Grim even by Oslo standards.

title: Smilla's Sense of Snow
description: A Greenlandic woman in Copenhagen reads a dead boy's footprints in the snow and knows he did not fall. Turns from investigation to Arctic expedition.

title: The Redbreast
description: A rare rifle surfaces in Oslo and the trail runs back to Norwegians who fought on the Eastern Front for the Germans. The best-plotted Harry Hole.

title: Faceless Killers
description: Kurt Wallander investigates a farm couple's murder while a dying word sets off attacks on refugees. The first Wallander, and it set the tone for the genre.

title: The Day of the Jackal
description: An English assassin is hired to kill de Gaulle, and a French detective has to find a man with no name. The suspense survives knowing de Gaulle died in bed.

title: The Bourne Identity
description: A man pulled from the Mediterranean with no memory and a Zurich account number discovers he is extremely good at violence. The template for a hundred imitators.

title: The Eagle Has Landed
description: German paratroopers land in a Norfolk village to kidnap Churchill. Higgins makes the Germans the protagonists and it works.

title: The Constant Gardener
description: A mild British diplomat in Nairobi investigates his activist wife's murder and finds a drug trial. Le Carré after the Cold War, angrier and less ambiguous.

title: A Perfect Spy
description: A senior intelligence officer disappears to a Devon boarding house and writes his life for his son. Le Carré's most autobiographical, built around a confidence-trickster father.

title: Slow Horses
description: MI5's failures are exiled to Slough House to do paperwork until they resign. A kidnapping gives them something real, which nobody wanted.

title: Killing Floor
description: Jack Reacher gets off a bus in a Georgia town and is arrested for a murder committed while he was on it. The first Reacher, and the counterfeiting plot is genuinely clever.

title: The Pelican Brief
description: A law student writes a speculative brief about two dead Supreme Court justices and people start dying around her.

title: The Client
description: An eleven-year-old witnesses a lawyer's suicide and learns where a senator's body is buried. He hires an attorney with a hundred dollars.

title: The Rainmaker
description: A new graduate with no clients takes an insurance company to trial over a denied leukaemia claim. Grisham's most convincing courtroom.

title: The Burden of Proof
description: A defence attorney comes home to find his wife dead in the garage and spends the book discovering what she was hiding. Turow's follow-up, and slower by design.

title: The Lincoln Lawyer
description: A defence attorney who works from the back of a town car gets a wealthy client and realises he may have failed an earlier one badly.

title: The Poet
description: A crime reporter investigating his twin brother's apparent suicide finds a pattern of detectives' deaths quoting Poe.

title: Shutter Island
description: Two US marshals go to a hospital for the criminally insane in 1954 Boston Harbor to find an escaped patient. Everything is exactly what it looks like, and is not.

title: Gone, Baby, Gone
description: Two private investigators look for a four-year-old taken from a Dorchester flat. The moral question at the end has no comfortable answer.

title: Red Dragon
description: A retired FBI profiler is brought back to catch a family annihilator and consults the man who nearly killed him. Lecter's first appearance, in a supporting part.

title: I Am Pilgrim
description: A retired intelligence officer is pulled back over a New York hotel murder that connects to a bioweapon plot. Very long, very propulsive.

title: The Martian
description: An astronaut left for dead on Mars keeps himself alive with botany and duct tape. Self-published first, and the arithmetic mostly checks out.

title: Project Hail Mary
description: A man wakes on a spacecraft with no memory, two dead crewmates, and a mission to save the sun. The first contact goes better than usual.

title: Dark Matter
description: A physics teacher is abducted and wakes in a life where he made the other choice. The premise escalates in a way that is hard to put down.

title: Recursion
description: People start remembering lives they did not live. A detective and a neuroscientist work out what a memory chair has done to causality.

title: The Passage
description: A military virus trial produces something that empties North America, then jumps ninety years to a colony running out of batteries. Vast and unusually well written for the shelf.

title: Swan Song
description: Nuclear war, and survivors converging on a child who can heal. Frequently compared to The Stand and rather nastier.

title: The Stand
description: A weaponised flu kills most of America and the survivors are drawn to either a Nebraska farmhouse or Las Vegas. King's longest and his most ambitious.

title: It
description: Seven children fight something in a Maine town's sewers, then return as adults having forgotten it. The childhood half is why it endures.

title: Misery
description: A romance novelist crashes his car and is nursed by his self-described number one fan, who does not like how the last book ended. Two rooms and a typewriter.

title: Pet Sematary
description: A burial ground behind a Maine house returns what is buried in it, changed. King held it back for years because he thought it went too far.

title: 'Salem's Lot
description: Dracula relocated to a Maine town that nobody outside would notice emptying. King's second novel and his most straightforwardly frightening.

title: The Exorcist
description: A film star's daughter deteriorates in ways medicine cannot explain and a Jesuit losing his faith is called. The medical procedures are the worst part.

title: Rosemary's Baby
description: A young wife in a Manhattan building becomes pregnant and cannot get anyone to take her fears seriously. The horror is the not being believed.

title: The Stepford Wives
description: A photographer moves to a Connecticut town where the women are uniformly serene and domestic. A hundred and forty pages and it added a word to the language.

title: Mexican Gothic
description: A 1950s Mexico City socialite visits her cousin at an English family's decaying silver-mining house in the mountains. The house is doing something.

title: The Only Good Indians
description: Four Blackfeet men are pursued a decade after an illegal elk hunt. Horror that takes the entity's grievance seriously.

title: The Twisted Ones
description: A woman clearing her dead grandmother's hoarder house in North Carolina finds a journal and, behind the treeline, the thing it describes.

title: Bird Box
description: Something outside drives anyone who sees it to kill. A woman rows two children down a river blindfolded. The withholding is the whole device.

title: The Troop
description: A scoutmaster and five boys on a Canadian island meet a starving man carrying an engineered parasite. Genuinely difficult to read in places.

title: Borne
description: A scavenger in a ruined city finds something growing on the flank of a giant flying bear and raises it. Stranger and warmer than that sounds.

title: The Girl with All the Gifts
description: A gifted child is strapped into a wheelchair at gunpoint every morning to go to lessons. A fungal apocalypse told from the wrong side of it.

title: World War Z
description: An oral history of a zombie war, country by country. The form lets Brooks write about logistics, quarantine politics and refugee flows rather than gore.

title: The Name of the Wind
description: A legendary figure running an inn under another name tells his own story over three days. Beautifully written, and the trilogy remains unfinished.

title: The Way of Kings
description: A world scoured by storms, an army of bridge-carrying slaves, and a magic system with rules Sanderson intends to hold for ten volumes.

title: Mistborn: The Final Empire
description: A thieving crew plans to rob a god-emperor whose prophesied hero already failed a thousand years ago. Metal-based magic with strict costs, which is the appeal.

title: The Lies of Locke Lamora
description: Con artists in a Venice-like city work a long fraud on the nobility while something worse moves through the underworld. Very funny until it is not.

title: The Blade Itself
description: A crippled Inquisitor, a vain duellist and a barbarian who wants to stop. Abercrombie takes epic fantasy's furniture and makes everyone worse.

title: Before They Are Hanged
description: A siege, a doomed quest and a losing campaign in the north, all going badly at once. The middle volume, and the bleakest.

title: Prince of Thorns
description: A thirteen-year-old prince leading a company of murderers back toward the father who let his mother die. Narrated by him, and he is not redeemed.

title: The Black Company
description: A mercenary company's annalist records a campaign for a side that is plainly evil. Written in a flat soldier's voice, and it invented grimdark.

title: The Last Wish
description: Linked stories introducing Geralt of Rivia, a mutant monster-hunter who keeps finding the monster is a person. Polish fairy tales, turned.

title: The Obelisk Gate
description: The second Broken Earth novel, in an underground comm during a season that may not end. Won the Hugo, as did the books either side of it.

title: The Priory of the Orange Tree
description: An eight-hundred-page standalone with two dragon traditions, a queen who must produce an heir, and a hidden order of mages. Deliberately not a series.

title: Piranesi
description: A man lives in an infinite house of statues and tides, keeping meticulous journals, and is certain there are only two people in the world. Short and remarkable.

title: The Night Circus
description: Two magicians are bound as children to a duel neither understands, staged inside a circus that appears without warning. Atmosphere well ahead of plot, on purpose.

title: The Ten Thousand Doors of January
description: A ward of a wealthy collector finds a book about doors between worlds and recognises her own life in it. Nested narratives, and pointed about who collects what.

title: The City We Became
description: New York's five boroughs each incarnate as a person to defend the city being born. Jemisin arguing directly with Lovecraft's politics.

title: The Rook
description: A woman wakes in a London park surrounded by bodies with a letter from her previous self explaining that she runs a supernatural civil service.

title: Rivers of London
description: A probationary constable takes a witness statement from a ghost and is apprenticed to the Met's last wizard. Police procedural with river goddesses.

title: Storm Front
description: Chicago's only professional wizard, listed in the phone book, consults for the police on a double murder by magic. Hardboiled detective with a staff.

title: Good Omens
description: An angel and a demon who have grown fond of England try to stop the apocalypse, having misplaced the Antichrist eleven years ago.

title: Guards! Guards!
description: The Ankh-Morpork Night Watch, three men and a dog, against a summoned dragon and a plot to restore the monarchy. The best entry point to Discworld.

title: Small Gods
description: A great god is reduced to a tortoise because only one person still actually believes in him. Pratchett's sharpest book about institutions and faith.

title: Night Watch
description: Commander Vimes is thrown back thirty years and has to mentor his younger self through a revolution he already knows the ending of. The darkest Discworld.

title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
description: Earth is demolished for a bypass and the last Englishman is rescued by a researcher for a guidebook. Every joke in it has been quoted to death and still works.

title: Uprooted
description: A village girl taken by the wizard who guards the valley turns out to be the wrong choice, and the corrupted Wood is worse than anyone admits. Polish folklore throughout.

title: Spinning Silver
description: A moneylender's daughter who turns silver into gold attracts the attention of a winter king. Rumpelstiltskin rebuilt around debt, antisemitism and cold.

title: The Bear and the Nightingale
description: A girl in medieval northern Rus can see the household spirits her stepmother's priest is determined to starve out. Russian folklore, and the winter is a character.

title: The Goblin Emperor
description: The despised half-goblin fourth son inherits an empire after an airship crash and has to govern a court that despises him. Almost entirely protocol, and gripping.

title: Gideon the Ninth
description: Necromancers and their swordsmen are summoned to a decaying palace to solve trials nobody explains. Lesbian necromancers in space, and it means it.

title: A Memory Called Empire
description: An ambassador arrives at a vast empire's capital carrying an outdated copy of her murdered predecessor's memories in her head. Won the Hugo.

title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
description: The crew of a tunnelling ship take a long job to a dangerous system. Almost plotless by design; the point is the people sharing the galley.

title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
description: A tea monk meets the first robot seen since they gained consciousness and walked into the forest centuries ago. It wants to know what people need.

title: All Systems Red
description: A security android that has hacked its own governor module wants mainly to be left alone with its serials. The clients keep nearly dying instead.

title: Children of Time
description: A terraforming experiment fails upward and uplifts spiders instead of monkeys, while the last humans arrive in a failing ark. Millennia of spider civilisation, told seriously.

title: The Dark Forest
description: Humanity has four centuries before the fleet arrives and can be read by the enemy's particles at all times, except inside its own head. The dark forest hypothesis in full.

title: Blindsight
description: A crew including a resurrected vampire investigates an object at the edge of the solar system that may be intelligent without being conscious. Bleak and heavily footnoted.
